item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 232300
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Fri Oct 23 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Vance, located several hundred miles south-southwest of Acapulco,
Mexico.

Western Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form near the International
Date Line, several hundred miles west of Johnston Atoll late this
weekend or early next week. Environmental conditions could support
some slow development thereafter while the system moves generally
eastward to east-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.title: Hurricane Vance Public Advisory Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Fri Oct 23 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 240245
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Vance Advisory Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 PM CST Fri Oct 23 2026
 
...VANCE NEAR MAJOR HURRICANE STRENGTH...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM CST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...12.0N 102.6W
ABOUT 385 MI...615 KM SSW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 495 MI...800 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...110 MPH...175 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 345 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...965 MB...28.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern coast of Mexico should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM CST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Vance was located
near latitude 12.0 North, longitude 102.6 West. Vance is moving
toward the north-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h), and this motion is
expected to continue through the weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 110 mph (175 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Some additional strengthening is possible through tonight. 
However, gradual weakening is forecast to begin by Saturday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles
(335 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 965 mb (28.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Vance are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico this
weekend and continue into next week. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Vance Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Fri Oct 23 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 240246
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Vance Discussion Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 PM CST Fri Oct 23 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that Vance became better organized 
earlier this evening, with cloud-top temperatures cooling and deep 
convection expanding around a warming eye. However, the eye has 
become less distinct during the past hour or two, with some warming 
of the cloud tops in the eyewall, possibly due to moderate southerly 
vertical wind shear. The subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from 
TAFB was T5.5/102 kt, although recent objective intensity estimates 
have trended downward toward 95 kt. Given the recent degradation in 
satellite presentation and the latest objective estimates, the 
initial intensity is set at 95 kt.
 
Vance is moving north-northwestward, or 345/6 kt. This general 
motion is expected to continue during the next couple of days as a 
broad mid- to upper-level trough evolves over the western portion of 
the United States, weakening the subtropical ridge over Mexico. 
Although the track guidance remains in relatively good agreement 
through 24 to 36 h, forecast confidence decreases thereafter as the 
trough shifts eastward and Vance enters a region of weaker steering 
currents. Significant cross-track spread persists among the guidance 
solutions, partly due to differences in how well Vance maintains its 
vertical structure as increasing shear affects the cyclone. A 
weaker, more vertically tilted system could be steered farther 
westward, while a stronger, vertically coupled hurricane would be 
more likely to continue northward toward the southwestern or 
west-central coast of Mexico. Given these persistent differences, 
the NHC track forecast remains largely unchanged from the previous, 
lying close to the HCCA and GDMI aids.
 
Vance may have reached its peak intensity earlier this evening after 
rapidly intensifying from 60 to 100 kt during the past 24 h. 
Although some additional strengthening is possible in the short 
term, recent satellite trends suggest that the hurricane may be 
beginning to feel the effects of a less favorable environment. 
Cooler sea surface temperatures associated with the wakes of recent 
tropical cyclones have reduced the ocean heat content along portions 
of Vance's forecast track. These cooler waters, combined with 
increasing vertical wind shear, should contribute to a weakening 
trend during the next day or two. However, the magnitude of 
weakening remains uncertain and will depend partly on how long Vance 
remains over the cooler waters. The aforementioned differences in 
the track guidance have also contributed to considerable spread 
among the intensity solutions, with the possibility of more 
substantial weakening than currently forecast. Vance could move 
north of the cooler waters by 48 h, allowing for some 
restrengthening. Thereafter, increasing vertical wind shear, 
decreasing mid-level moisture, and possible land interaction should 
lead to another weakening trend late in the forecast period. The NHC 
intensity forecast remains similar to the previous prediction and 
lies near the upper end of the guidance envelope through much of the 
forecast period.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  24/0300Z 12.0N 102.6W   95 KT 110 MPH
 12H  24/1200Z 12.8N 102.8W  105 KT 120 MPH
 24H  25/0000Z 13.8N 103.1W  100 KT 115 MPH
 36H  25/1200Z 14.8N 103.4W   90 KT 105 MPH

120H  29/0000Z 18.4N 104.4W   70 KT  80 MPH
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs
